targetTexts.1: Woe is me! For I am like one gathering summer fruit at the gleaning of the vineyard; there is no cluster to eat, no early fig that I crave.
targetTexts.2: The godly man has perished from the earth; there is no one upright among men. They all lie in wait for blood; they hunt one another with a net.
targetTexts.3: Both hands are skilled at evil; the prince and the judge demand a bribe. When the powerful utters his evil desire, they all conspire together.
targetTexts.4: The best of them is like a brier; the most upright is sharper than a hedge of thorns. The day for your watchmen has come, the day of your visitation. Now is the time of their confusion.
targetTexts.5: Do not rely on a friend; do not trust in a companion. Seal the doors of your mouth from her who lies in your arms.
targetTexts.6: For a son dishonors his father, a daughter rises against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law. A man’s enemies are the members of his own household.
targetTexts.7: But as for me, I will look to the LORD; I will wait for the God of my salvation. My God will hear me.
targetTexts.8: Do not gloat over me, my enemy! Though I have fallen, I will arise; though I sit in darkness, the LORD will be my light.
targetTexts.9: Because I have sinned against Him, I must endure the rage of the LORD, until He argues my case and executes justice for me. He will bring me into the light; I will see His righteousness.
targetTexts.10: Then my enemy will see and will be covered with shame—she who said to me, “Where is the LORD your God?” My eyes will see her; at that time she will be trampled like mud in the streets.
targetTexts.11: The day for rebuilding your walls will come—the day for extending your boundary.
targetTexts.12: On that day they will come to you from Assyria and the cities of Egypt, even from Egypt to the Euphrates, from sea to sea and mountain to mountain.
targetTexts.13: Then the earth will become desolate because of its inhabitants, as the fruit of their deeds.
targetTexts.14: Shepherd with Your staff Your people, the flock of Your inheritance. They live alone in a woodland, surrounded by pastures. Let them graze in Bashan and Gilead, as in the days of old.
targetTexts.15: As in the days when you came out of Egypt, I will show My wonders.
targetTexts.16: Nations will see and be ashamed, deprived of all their might. They will put their hands over their mouths, and their ears will become deaf.
targetTexts.17: They will lick the dust like a snake, like reptiles slithering on the ground. They will come trembling from their strongholds in the presence of the LORD our God; they will tremble in fear of You.
targetTexts.18: Who is a God like You, who pardons iniquity and passes over the transgression of the remnant of His inheritance—who does not retain His anger forever, because He delights in loving devotion?
targetTexts.19: He will again have compassion on us; He will vanquish our iniquities. You will cast out all our sins into the depths of the sea.
targetTexts.20: You will show faithfulness to Jacob and loving devotion to Abraham, as You swore to our fathers from the days of old.
